title: CHAPTER THIRTY-FOUR. On the governance of angels
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-FOUR. On the governance of angels.

Next, the special governance of GOD is of ANGELS or of HUMAN BEINGS. II. The governance of angels is that by which they are governed by GOD only spiritually. Their governance must be considered here because God variously uses their ministry concerning human beings (Psalm 91:11 and 34:8; Isaiah 37:36; Hebrews 1:14) and other creatures that serve humankind.

III. It is the conservation of their essence and the direction of their actions. IV. Conservation of their essence is that by which each is eternalized without propagation. For they are spirits, and so incorporeal, created immediately by God from nothing, as shown above in chapter 26, and not made for generating (Matthew 22:30). Actions is the prescription of law and the ordination of the    event that follows from it.

title: VI. Angelic law and five offices: singers, orators, ambassadors, protectors, war-leaders
english: VI. That law is that by which obedience is required of them — the same in substance as the Decalogue prescribed to human beings. Yet here must be excepted all that regards either the nature of the human body or the condition of this mortal life: many duties of the second and fourth commandments; many of inferiors toward superiors, as of children toward parents in the fifth; many concerning the propagation of the race in the seventh; and some concerning the way of gaining livelihood in the eighth — which do not suit them.

The offices of angels are roughly fivefold. They are first singers, second orators, third ambassadors, fourth protectors, fifth war-leaders. Their first and chief task is always to love God and never cease praising Him; they so love that they burn for God, and so love that with a sleepless harmony of praise they praise Him together. Who will make the concert of heaven sleep? Job asks (38:37). Otherwise in heaven the angels sing and make the pleasure of their music more lasting: they begin and never leave off; they satisfy and create no weariness. Isaiah heard and wrote the words of that heavenly oratory (chapter 6), where the Seraphim cried one to another: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God of hosts; the whole earth is full of His glory.

Their second office: they are orators (Revelation 8:3). Third: ambassadors in affairs of highest moment. Fourth: they are protectors (Psalm 91). Fifth: they are war-leaders, and such that whenever they will they have victory standing on their side (Exodus 23:20; Joshua 5).

title: VII–X. Ordination of events: preservation, confirmation, permission of fall, hardening; good angels works
english: VII. Ordination of the event is preservation, confirmation, or permission of a fall and hardening. VIII. Preservation is that by which certain angels are kept from falling. IX. Confirmation is that by which they are made firm in the good.

X. There are many modes by which good angels work concerning human beings: they open tongues and hand on divine speech (Isaiah 6:6); they heal the sick (John 5:4); they refresh the weary (1 Kings 19:7); they allow themselves to be overcome by the dear (Genesis 32:28); they console the afflicted (Genesis 21:17); they exhort to doing good (Acts 8:26); they pass from heaven to earth (Genesis 28:12; John 1:51); they animate those who pray (Judges 13); they love and defend the chaste everywhere most ardently (Judith 13:20).

It may be asked why no holy angel (so far as I know) has ever seated himself in a dear human body, though fugitive angels have so often dared it. I answer: first, the human being is a temple sacred to the Deity; angels, led by reverence and love, refuse to invade their Princes chamber by their own entry. Second, since God so ennobled human origin by the wondrous conjunction of divine and human nature, angels will claim so little license over a human being that they endure to be called not only servants of the Deity but servants of the human as well.

title: XI. Canons concerning good angels and their governance
english: XI. Canons are to be observed concerning good angels and their governance. First, the confirmation of angels in the good was not a wages owed to some merit, but the free reward of most liberal God (Romans 11:35). Second, angels serve each person and each order (Psalm 34:8). Third, a human being has not only one guardian angel but many at once (Psalm 91:11; Matthew 18:10; Acts 12:15; Zanchi). Fourth, angels are not to be adored (Revelation 19:10). Fifth, angels turn away from whatever smells of vice; yet among vices they most hate heat, smoke, and stench — the heat of anger and envy, the smoke of pride, the stench of luxury.

title: XII–XIII. Permission and hardening of fallen angels; names of unclean spirits
english: XII. Permission is that by which, with divine power temporarily set aside, certain angels are allowed to fall. XIII. Hardening at by which the fallen, grace denied, are made firm in evil.

They are also called unclean spirits (Luke 11:24), worthless spirits (1 Kings 16:14), spirits of error (1 Timothy 4:1), Satan, the Devil, the ancient serpent, the dragon, angels of Satan (Revelation 12:9), father of the lie (John 8:44), spiritual wickedness (Ephesians 6:12), roaring lion (1 Peter 5:8), demons (Luke 11), satyrs (Leviticus 17:7), hairy ones (Isaiah 13:21; 34:14). The reason for the naming is that they are spirits created by God indeed, but who by free will fell away at the beginning from the truth in which they were made, and became horrible adversaries of both God and human beings, and are kept in eternal chains for judgment (John 8:44; 2 Peter 2:4; Jude 6).

title: XIV. Canons concerning fallen angels; Cap. 34 close
english: XIV. Canons are to be noted concerning them. First, the Devil was evil from the beginning not of creation but of defection (Augustine; Thomas; Zanchi). Second, the impious are children of the Devil not with respect to their substance but in view of the accident of malice. Third, the Devil is the first author and fountain of sin — of malice both in his own nature and in the human race (John 8:44; 1 John 3:8). Fourth, fallen angels retained their substance with intellect and will, and great power besides, but by all these they are borne only to evil. Fifth, the Devil abuses intellect, will, power, and all his forces not only to propagate his malice but also to root out Gods kingdom.

Sixth, the Devil does not know human thoughts except through outward signs and probably, or impure ones that he himself suggests. Seventh, Satans power is great, but under Gods omnipotence. Eighth, the Devil can do wonders, but not true and properly so-called miracles. Ninth, the Devil does what he can when God permits; what he can, he does not do when God forbids. Tenth, no human being by his own powers can drive back the Devil and resist him; it is Gods grace and power alone to overcome him and to free the repentant and believing human being from his snares.
